units.title: Digital Citizenship & Online Identity
units.essentialQuestion: How does your digital footprint define who you are online and in the future?
units.description: Students explore responsible digital citizenship, online safety, and personal branding. They learn to evaluate online content critically and create a professional digital identity.

lessons.title: Course Introduction & Expectations
lessons.objective: Recall course expectations, class procedures, and technology lab safety rules.

lessons.title: Amazon Warehouse Virtual Tour
lessons.objective: Describe how technology is used in modern logistics and identify ICT career pathways.

lessons.title: Syllabus & Course Overview
lessons.objective: Summarize the course pathway, grading policies, and expectations for the two-year CTE program.

lessons.title: Google Interland – Digital Safety
lessons.objective: Apply strategies for staying safe online by navigating interactive scenarios about phishing, oversharing, and password security.

lessons.title: Fake Instagram Profile Analysis
lessons.objective: Evaluate fake social media profiles to distinguish credible from deceptive online identities.

lessons.title: Social Sleuth Investigation
lessons.objective: Analyze digital footprints to determine what personal information is publicly accessible.

lessons.title: Google Header Design
lessons.objective: Design a personalized Google Classroom header representing identity using basic graphic design principles.

units.title: Digital Portfolios & Personal Branding
units.essentialQuestion: How do you communicate your skills, identity, and goals to an authentic audience?
units.description: Students build and maintain a digital portfolio using Canva and Google Sites to document their learning journey. They set SMART goals and learn to present their work professionally.

lessons.title: Canva Header Design
lessons.objective: Create a professional-quality portfolio header using Canva, applying color theory and typography principles.

lessons.title: Digital Portfolio Setup
lessons.objective: Construct a digital portfolio site that organizes work samples, bio, and learning reflections.

lessons.title: Choose Your Own Adventure – Planning & Creation
lessons.objective: Design and develop an interactive choose-your-own-adventure story using hyperlinks and branching logic.

lessons.title: Digital Portfolio Goals (SMART Goals)
lessons.objective: Formulate SMART goals for the semester and articulate them within the digital portfolio.

units.title: Digital Image Editing with Photoshop
units.essentialQuestion: How do digital tools empower us to construct and communicate meaning through images?
units.description: Students develop proficiency in Adobe Photoshop, progressing from basic layer manipulation to advanced compositing techniques.

lessons.title: Photoshop Introduction & Interface
lessons.objective: Identify the key tools, panels, and workspace elements of the Photoshop interface.

lessons.title: Layers Assignment
lessons.objective: Demonstrate how layers function by composing a multi-layer image with proper ordering and opacity.

lessons.title: Lasso Tool Tracing & Assignment
lessons.objective: Apply selection tools to isolate and manipulate image elements with precision.

lessons.title: Digital Collage
lessons.objective: Create a digital collage by combining multiple image sources, demonstrating layer management and composition.

lessons.title: Lasso Leaves Project
lessons.objective: Apply lasso and selection tools to create a nature-themed composition with extracted elements.

lessons.title: Digital Filters & Effects
lessons.objective: Experiment with Photoshop filters to transform images and explain how filters modify pixel data.

lessons.title: Combining Images – Meme Creation
lessons.objective: Combine text and images to create original memes, applying typography and composition skills.

lessons.title: Digital Citizenship Meme
lessons.objective: Design a meme that communicates a digital citizenship concept.

units.title: Animated GIFs & Digital Media
units.essentialQuestion: How does motion and timing change how we communicate a message?
units.description: Students create animated GIFs using Photoshop's timeline feature, exploring motion, looping, and digital media concepts.

lessons.title: Animated GIF Introduction
lessons.objective: Explain how frame-based animation creates the illusion of motion in digital media.

lessons.title: GIF Creation Project
lessons.objective: Create an original animated GIF using Photoshop timeline, applying principles of motion and looping.

units.title: Game Design Project (Semester 1 Capstone)
units.essentialQuestion: What makes a game engaging, fair, and worth playing?
units.description: Students apply the full design process to create an original board or digital game, culminating in a class showcase.

lessons.title: Game Design Introduction & Process
lessons.objective: Identify the stages of the game design process and understand what makes a game engaging.

lessons.title: Game Design Document Creation
lessons.objective: Develop a comprehensive game design document outlining rules, mechanics, and player experience.

lessons.title: Game Prototype Development
lessons.objective: Build a playable prototype of the designed game and conduct initial playtesting.

lessons.title: Playtest & Revise
lessons.objective: Conduct structured playtesting sessions, collect feedback, and implement design revisions.

lessons.title: Game Showcase & Reflection
lessons.objective: Present the completed game to peers, articulate design decisions, and reflect on the design process.

units.title: Introduction to Programming with Scratch
units.essentialQuestion: How can sequencing and logic allow us to create something from nothing?
units.description: Students learn foundational programming concepts through Scratch: sequences, loops, events, and basic animation.

lessons.title: Scratch Interface & First Program
lessons.objective: Navigate the Scratch interface and create a simple program using sequences and events.

lessons.title: Loops & Repetition
lessons.objective: Implement loops in Scratch programs to create repetitive patterns and efficient code.

lessons.title: Events & Interactivity
lessons.objective: Use event-based programming to create interactive Scratch projects that respond to user input.

lessons.title: Scratch Animation Project
lessons.objective: Create an animated story in Scratch demonstrating sequences, loops, and event handling.

units.title: Animation & Storytelling with Scratch
units.essentialQuestion: How do we use code to tell a story that moves an audience?
units.description: Students combine programming skills with narrative thinking to create animated stories in Scratch, developing both technical and creative abilities.

lessons.title: Sprite Costumes & Animation
lessons.objective: Use sprite costumes and timing to create smooth character animations in Scratch.

lessons.title: Scene Design & Backgrounds
lessons.objective: Design multi-scene Scratch projects with background transitions and environment changes.

lessons.title: Animated Story Project
lessons.objective: Develop a multi-scene animated story in Scratch with a clear beginning, middle, and end.

units.title: Conditionals & Logic in Scratch
units.essentialQuestion: How does a computer make decisions, and how do those decisions shape what a program can do?
units.description: Students explore conditional logic and boolean expressions, applying them to create programs that make decisions and respond to conditions.

lessons.title: If/Then & Boolean Logic
lessons.objective: Explain how conditional statements allow programs to make decisions based on conditions.

lessons.title: Keyboard & Mouse Conditionals
lessons.objective: Implement keyboard and mouse input handlers using conditional logic in Scratch.

lessons.title: Conditional Mini-Project
lessons.objective: Create an interactive Scratch project that uses conditionals to create meaningful decision points.

units.title: Advanced Scratch: Variables & Game Design
units.essentialQuestion: How do variables transform a program from static to dynamic?
units.description: Students learn variables, score tracking, and advanced game mechanics, culminating in original game designs.

lessons.title: Variables Introduction
lessons.objective: Define variables and demonstrate how they store and change data within a program.

lessons.title: Score & Lives Systems
lessons.objective: Implement score and lives tracking systems using variables in a Scratch game.

lessons.title: Advanced Game Development
lessons.objective: Design and develop a complete arcade-style game in Scratch with variables, conditionals, and collision detection.

units.title: Semester 2 Capstone & Portfolio Showcase
units.essentialQuestion: What have you learned, created, and become this year?
units.description: Students compile their best work, reflect on growth across the year, and showcase their digital portfolio to an authentic audience.

lessons.title: Portfolio Curation & Selection
lessons.objective: Curate a digital portfolio by selecting and organizing best work samples with written reflections.

lessons.title: Portfolio Presentation Preparation
lessons.objective: Prepare a structured presentation of the digital portfolio for an authentic audience.

lessons.title: Portfolio Showcase Event
lessons.objective: Present the completed digital portfolio to peers, family, and community members, articulating learning growth.

lessons.title: Year-End Reflection
lessons.objective: Write a comprehensive reflection on learning growth, challenges overcome, and goals for next year.
